note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

Pull request #3038 carries this record. cinatra#1381 (epic #1373) plugs the memory PromotionBackend into the shared promotion approvals source, whose `memoryPromotionAdapter` shipped dormant (`backend: null`) for exactly this flow, and adds the `memory_promote_request` tool beside it. `from` is MAIN's own committed ceiling at 6c2147748ca40c09eaa7bbdf3ead65ce7f84daab (which this branch has merged).

WHAT THE RAISE IS, measured as a module SET and not only as a number: exactly EIGHT modules enter this route's graph and none leaves, and it is the SAME eight on all four routes this record covers.
SEVEN are the app's own net-new first-party modules, every one of them a file that does not exist on main:
  src/lib/objects/memory-promotion-request-schema.ts  — the request ledger's bootstrap DDL leaf (zero imports),
  src/lib/objects/memory-promotion-request-store.ts   — the ledger store + the advisory duplicate count,
  src/lib/objects/memory-row-promotion.ts             — the decide ladder and the one-transaction apply,
  src/lib/approvals/sources/memory-promotion.ts       — the PromotionBackend the dormant adapter was waiting for,
  src/lib/memory/memory-promotion-request.ts          — the one actor-gated request service,
  src/lib/memory/mcp.ts                               — the `memory_promote_request` tool module,
  src/lib/mcp-tool-scope.ts                           — the MCP scope resolver.
ONE is a workspace module: packages/memory/src/secret-scan.ts, the cinatra#1378 credential detector, REUSED by the approve gate rather than re-implemented — a promotion gate carrying its own regex set would drift away from the ingest gate and let through exactly what ingest refuses. The analyzer's byOwner split shows `@cinatra-ai/memory: 1` on each of these four routes where main had no such owner at all, which is what makes the 7+1 split measured rather than asserted.

NO BARREL IMPORT IS OPENED and no module leaves. `src/lib/mcp-tool-scope.ts` is a NET-NEW module, not a relocation that cancels: `resolveScope` moved out of src/lib/artifacts/mcp.ts (which stays in the graph and now imports it), so the honest accounting is +1 for the extraction, and it is counted as such above. It is extracted rather than copied because it is the A2A precedence rule, and a second copy of a precedence rule is how two tools end up disagreeing about whose organization a call runs in.

WHY THE GROWTH IS ACCEPTED. The shared promotion source is REACHED from these routes already (the artifact subject landed in #1437), so a second subject cannot be added without its backend joining that graph; and the request tool has to be registered on the MCP server to exist at all. The DECISION half adds nothing: approve and reject ride the already-registered `approvals_*` tools over the same source, so this slice ships one tool and no decide primitive.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED, the way CI measures: with the companion extension fleet cloned PINNED (112/112 at their lock SHAs) and missingCount 0 on EVERY tracked route, using an unmodified scripts/route-graph.mjs. Main's four committed ceilings are 1730 / 1831 / 1735 / 1745 and this merged tree measures 1738 / 1839 / 1743 / 1753 — the same +8 on each, with the same owner split. On /chat the +8 rides on top of pull request #3014's own +4 (the HITL screen card modules), which is already INSIDE main's committed 1831; the two module sets are disjoint.
